title: Public endpoint capacity offset scenarios — Q3 2026
content:
Purpose:
Quick-run capacity offset scenarios for the public inference endpoint (aka public endpoint) oriented around latency-SLA driven headroom. This sheet focuses on tokens/sec and QPS peaks by region, the GPU families we expect to allocate, and how many reserve GPUs (safety slices) to keep hot to preserve p99 latency under sudden bursts.

Scope / assumptions:
- Time horizon: Q3 2026 planning window (Jul–Sep).
- Models in scope: chat-large (L2, ~45 tokens/sec per request average), instruction-medium (M1), embed-small (E1).
- Typical request mix (by token consumption): chat-large 60%, instruction-medium 25%, embed-small 15%.
- Average tokens per call: chat-large 450, instruction-medium 120, embed-small 32.
- KV cache hit rate: baseline 28% (improvements expected to 35% with prefix caching).
- Pre-warm/container spin-up lead time: 18–30s for cold A100 pods, 6–12s for H100 optimized pools.
- Target utilization: 70% sustained, 85% short-term burst allowable; reserve capacity required to maintain p99 latency SLO.
- Cost note: H100 capacity is ~1.6x faster (tokens/sec) than A100 for our compiled kernels on chat-large; L4 used for embedding-only fleet.

Regional baseline peak (observed last 4 weeks) — working numbers for planning:
- NA (us-east/us-west combined): 145k tokens/sec baseline peak (obs 2026-05), ~310 QPS weighted by model mix
- EU (eu-west + eu-central): 62k tokens/sec baseline peak, ~135 QPS
- APAC (singapore + syd): 39k tokens/sec baseline peak, ~78 QPS

Scenarios (tokens/sec presented are net of current caching but pre-regen of improved cache):
1) Conservative growth + 25% marketing campaign burst (30-day tail)
   - NA peak: 145k * 1.25 = 181k tps -> target headroom = +30% => 235k tps
   - EU peak: 62k * 1.25 = 77.5k -> headroom => 101k tps
   - APAC peak: 39k * 1.25 = 48.75k -> headroom => 63k tps
   GPU translation (nominal tokens/sec per GPU at 70% util):
   - H100 (chat-optimized): 18k tps/GPU
   - A100-80GB (mixed): 11.5k tps/GPU
   - L4 (embed-only): 3.2k tps/GPU
   Allocation suggestion:
   - NA: prefer H100 heavy: target H100=10 GPUs (180k), buffer with A100=5 GPUs (57.5k) -> planned pool = 15 GPUs (combined capacity ~237.5k tps)
   - EU: A100 primary: A100=9 GPUs (103.5k tps) -> planned pool = 9 GPUs (meets 101k tps)
   - APAC: A100=4 GPUs (46k) + L4=5 (16k embedding offload) -> combined ~62k tps -> planned pool = 9 GPUs

2) Worst-case sudden traffic storm (2x baseline for 15 minutes) - planned automated fallback policy
   - Rule: if tokens/sec > 1.7x baseline for > 60s, route non-critical traffic to cheaper-model fallback and divert to dedicated burst pool.
   - NA worst: 290k tps -> fallback target reduce compute demand by 40% -> effective demand 174k tps -> served by existing planned pool + 4 hot reserve H100s for p99

Hot reserve (safety slices) policy recommendations:
- Keep at least 10% of region capacity reserved as hot pre-warmed GPUs (not billed to customers). For NA that is ~1.5 GPUs equivalent -> round up to 2 H100 hot reserve due to discrete slices.
- EU: 9 GPU pool -> reserve 1 A100 hot. APAC: reserve 1 A100 + 1 L4 for embed spikes.

Pre-warm and autoscale knobs (operational parameters):
- Prewarm threshold: if rolling 10m increase > 20% trigger +2 pre-warm containers per 50k tps growth.
- Scale step: add GPUs in slices of 1 (A100/H100) or 2 (L4) with cooldown 90s.
- Warmup hold: once scale completes, keep additional slices for 5m to stabilize traffic patterns before retiring.

Tail-latency driven headroom math (p99 guardrail):
- Observed p99 degradation when server util > 88% for A100 pools. We choose target sustained util 70% -> headroom fraction = (1 - 0.7) / 0.7 = 42% overhead relative to load.
- Practically we apply a 30% headroom on top of forecast burst for cost balance, plus discrete rounding to GPU slices -> results in ~+30% planning factor in scenarios above.

Model variant fallback matrix (how we buy headroom with model swaps):
- chat-large -> chat-medium (quantized) reduces tps by ~42% and increases per-token latency slightly but preserves p95; use for non-payment critical routes.
- instruction-medium -> instruction-small (fast) reduces demand by ~35%.
- embed-small always routed to L4 unless CPU fallback necessary.

Cost impact estimate (monthly run rate delta for planned pools vs baseline):
- NA: +5 H100 equivalent vs baseline -> delta est $88k/mo (on-cloud list rates) assuming reserved discount ~20% for committed purchase
- EU: +3 A100 equivalents -> delta est $22k/mo
- APAC: +4 mixed GPUs -> delta est $26k/mo
Note: finance to produce exact commitment amortization; these are top-level engineering working numbers.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm improvement timeline for prefix cache (35% hit target) and recompute nets for each scenario (Diego to own).
- Validate H100 performance numbers on release-compiler branch (PR: gh/pr/infra/1127). Marcus to run benchmark suite next week.
- Determine whether pre-warm lease model should be per-customer or pooled global slices for multi-tenant optimization.
- Confirm fallback model quality gates with product / trust & safety for public endpoint usage.

Operational checklist for on-call SREs (short form):
- When p95 latency climbs > 2x baseline: inspect GPU util and p50/p95 CPU spin; if util >80%, kick immediate scale + pre-warm policy.
- If a region hits 1.5x planned pool capacity: enable fallbacks, open triage channel (#infra-capacity), page infra-oncall.
- Post-incident runbook: capture model mix, tokens/sec, KV cache hit rate, exact GPU billing window, and retention for 90 days.

Notes (informal):
- This is a working doc for PM/infra sync. Expect updates after Marcus' microbenchmarks and Diego's cache sim.
- I intentionally used mixed GPU counts to reflect existing contractual limits in EU (A100-heavy). If we can renegotiate region mix before Q3, shifting 2 A100->H100 in NA yields ~+36% token throughput for little added orchestration complexity.
